text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- European telecommunication companies should intensify strategic cooperation to compete with U.S. and Japanese manufacturers, said Ericsson CEO Lars Ramqvist.
- Shortening working hours is out of question in the next round of pay talks, says Jukka Harmala, managing director of Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).
- A decision to join EMU must be made through a law not a government statement, Centre Party leader Esko Aho says. @
- A clear majority of Social Democrat MPs support Finnish EMU membership of EMU, says Erkki Tuomioja, leader of the party parliamentary group.
- Finnish people oppose EMU more than other EU nationals - only 29 percent are in favour, European Commission poll shows.
- Leftist Alliance will leave goverment on EMU "over my dead body", says Claes Andersson, party head and Culture Minister who is 60 today.
- Tax on wines may be reduced already next year, Second Finance Minister Arja Alho says. @
- About 40 Finnish investment projects in Russia are waiting for a new guarantee agreement due to be signed in June, says Matti Vuoria, chief secretary at Trade and Industry Ministry.
- Finland has too few small and middle sized companies and risks losing subcontracts abroad, says Johannes Koroma, chairman of Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen wants committee investigating Estonia disaster to finish work without delays. @
- Lipponen finds it cheeky that company managers arrange share options for each other.
- Three of the new euro coins will contain metal from Outokumpu.
- Profitability of big Finnish industrial companies is at the same high level as 1994, Statistics Finland study shows.
